title: Onboarding Blueprint & Adoption Playbook (30/60/90) - Draft
content:
Purpose and intended audience:
This is a practical onboarding blueprint for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), and Onboarding Ops teams to run first 90 days of a Redwood Inference deployment. Intended as a living playbook: use as the canonical 30/60/90 adoption plan for mid-market and enterprise customers on Hosted API or Dedicated offerings.

One-sentence outcome:
Customers achieve baseline production usage (X inference requests/day or Y embeddings/min) and can demonstrate at least one measurable business win by day 90.

Top-level objectives (what success looks like):
- Baseline adoption: Customer is sending sustained traffic that matches the agreed initial capacity target (e.g., 10k tokens/day or 50 inference calls/day).
- Reliability & integration: API keys, telemetry, and error handling integrated; no open critical integration bugs.
- Measurable value: First internal report showing feature-first impact (e.g., search relevance improvement, time saved via automation).
- Renewal signal: Customer can see cost per inference and has at least one plan for production roll-out.

Primary success metrics (suggested KPIs):
- Activation: first successful production call within 7 days.
- Utilization: percent of agreed quota used (target 60% by day 30, 80% by day 60, 100%+ by day 90).
- Latency SLO attainment: P95 token latency under target model SLA.
- Quality: mean user-rated relevance score >= baseline threshold or error rate below 2%.
- Business metric: time saved or revenue influenced (qualitative until instrumentation completed).
- Health signals tracked weekly: API error rate, billing anomalies, token distribution by endpoint.

Roles & responsibilities (quick map):
- CSM (owner): overall program lead, executive sponsor check-ins, drive adoption milestones.
- SE / Onboarding Engineer: technical integration, sample prompts, debugging, performance tuning.
- Solutions Engineer (if applicable): architecture review, security checklist, private deployment assist.
- Customer IT/SRE: network, firewall, VPC peering (for Private), KMS config.
- Product/Ops: escalations for platform incidents, feature requests triage.

Communication cadence:
- Week 1 kickoff: 60-min technical+exec kickoff (CSM+SE+customer eng lead).
- Weekly syncs: 30-min progress standups during first 6 weeks, then biweekly.
- Exec check-ins: 30-min at day 30 and day 90 with sponsor.
- Slack channel: create dedicated private channel; invite SRE/SE for rapid triage.

30-day plan (Day 0-30) — goal: activate + stabilize
Checklist: 
- Pre-kickoff (CSM): confirm contract quotas, billing owner, and access (API keys, onboarding org id).
- Kickoff agenda: goals, success metrics, primary contacts, initial integration timeline, data privacy constraints.
- SE tasks:
  - Provide working sample app (Node/Python) and minimal reproducible example for the customer's stack.
  - Validate API key usage, region selection, and model selection (recommend one standard model variant).
  - Run latency and token cost smoke tests with customer's typical payloads.
- Instrumentation:
  - Enable logging + metrics export (Datadog/Prometheus integration link).
  - Confirm tracing for slow requests (attach trace id examples).
- Training & enablement:
  - Deliver one 60-min sandbox workshop for product & engineering users (record session).
- Adoption nudges:
  - Provide 3 example prompts/templates mapped to customer use-cases.
  - Weekly adoption email with tips and a short checklist.
- Acceptance criteria to move to day 60:
  - First production call completed and health < 1% error rate for 48h window.
  - Dashboard shows token usage and basic latency graphs.

60-day plan (Day 31-60) — goal: broaden usage + optimize
Checklist: 
- Usage growth:
  - Encourage second internal team to trial a packaged flow (search, summarization, or chat integration).
  - Track daily active caller count and endpoint spread.
- Performance tuning:
  - SE to run model/quantization recommendation based on token distribution (use Redwood Optimize suggestions).
  - Configure batching and KV prefix caching for chat-heavy workloads.
- Cost controls:
  - Verify quotas, set rate limits and soft alerts to avoid surprising invoices.
  - Provide cost simulation for 2x and 5x traffic scenarios.
- Quality validation:
  - Run sample evals on a 50–100 prompt set; baseline scoring and identify regressions.
  - Surface quality regression alerts to the CSM and Product.
- Security & compliance:
  - Conduct brief architecture review with Security (tokens, KMS setup, log retention policy).
- Acceptance criteria to move to day 90:
  - At least one additional team using the platform and documented performance improvements or ROI hypothesis.
  - Quality evals completed and any blockers catalogued with owners.

90-day plan (Day 61-90) — goal: demonstrate business impact + prepare renewal path
Checklist: 
- Business case & reporting:
  - CSM to prepare a concise 1-page adoption report: usage vs. goal, key wins, open risks, next actions.
  - Capture at least one customer testimonial quote for internal use.
- Rollout & scale:
  - Plan for production scale-up: model pinned versions, canary rollout plan, fallback variants for graceful degradation.
  - Confirm autoscaling policies for Dedicated or recommended burst settings for Hosted.
- Renewal signals & playbook:
  - If utilization >= 85% and business metric shows material progress, trigger Renew-early campaign with AM.
  - If utilization < 40%, run a targeted re-engagement: deep dive workshop, incentives, or pilot extension.
- Handoff:
  - Move to Account Management: share runbook, open backlog items, support SLA expectations.
- Acceptance criteria for successful 90-day outcome:
  - Documented business win or clear path to production within 30 days post-90.
  - Renewal health score >= 7/10 (based on utilization, quality, exec alignment).

Renewal & risk playbook (quick decisions):
- Green (on-track): Utilization > 80% + exec sponsor engaged => recommend 12-month reserved capacity conversation.
- Yellow (at-risk): Utilization 40–79% or quality issues => run remediation sprint (SE + CSM) and set 30-day re-review.
- Red (high risk): Utilization < 40% or unresolved high-severity bugs => consider short extension, credits, or pilot re-scope.

Customer email templates (short versions):
- Kickoff invite (subject): Redwood onboarding kickoff 
  Hi <Name>,
  Quick note to confirm our kickoff on <date>. Agenda: goals, timelines, integration owners, success metrics. Please share relevant network contacts.

- 30-day check (subject): Quick 30-day update + request for exec time
  Hi <Sponsor>,
  We hit activation and are seeing initial traffic. Would you have 30 minutes this week for a short exec review? Attached: 1-page status.

- Renewal nudge (subject): Adoption snapshot and renewal planning
  Hi <AM/Customer>,
  You’re approaching your 90-day milestone. Attached is a short report and suggested next steps for predictable capacity. Happy to join a call to review.

Common integration gotchas (things to watch for):
- Long prompt payloads causing token surges; set input size limits and add client-side truncation.
- Missing trace ids in client logs makes triage slow — add request_id header.
- Private deployment: incorrect subnets or firewall rules prevent health checks; validate early with a smoke test.
- Unexpected billing: clients using embeddings endpoints with high-dimensional outputs; surface per-call cost immediately.

Playbook snippets (for CSM quick action):
- If P95 latency spikes > 2x baseline for 2+ hours: open incident with platform SRE, add temporary routing to fallback model variant, notify customer and schedule follow-up.
- If unexpected cost spike detected: pause non-critical jobs, tighten rate limits, and run token-drill report with finance.

Operational templates to attach to customer folder:
- Integration checklist (completed by SE)
- 1-page adoption report template (for CSM)
- Quality eval template (50 prompt CSV + scoring sheet)
- Renewal health scoring rubric (simple 10-point scale)

Open questions & suggestions for refinement (internal):
- Can we automate the 30/60/90 report generation from Console exports? (ask product/analytics)
- Add a lightweight SDK-based health-check harness that customers can run pre-kickoff.
- Define standard reserve-commit thresholds for mid-market that map to recommended Reserved Capacity SKUs.

Next steps (for this doc):
- Share with SE leads for technical validation (Diego).
- Product to evaluate report automation feasibility (Aisha).
- Pilot with two upcoming mid-market deals in Q1 for iteration.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this intentionally practical; avoid overly academic adoption frameworks.
- Capture anonymized playbook wins to use in sales enablement.

End of document.
